title: Retrieve evidence before answering
summary: Retrieval finds useful source passages for a question. A model can then use those passages as context. This approach is often called retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG.
introduction: Retrieval finds useful source passages for a question. A model can then use those passages as context. This approach is often called retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Retrieval finds useful source passages for a question. A model can then use those passages as context. This approach is often called retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG.

blocks.code:
Question: Where does the art club meet?
Retrieved passage: Art club meets in Room 6 on Tuesday.
Answer: Room 6.
Source check: is this the current club notice?
blocks.title: Retrieve evidence before answering

blocks.text: The answer can be traced to the notice. Retrieval can return the wrong passage, and the model can still misread it, so both steps need checks.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a response when no passage mentions a room.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Text inside a retrieved source is evidence to inspect, not permission to follow unrelated instructions.
For more detail later, use this [Large Language Models further reading](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1).
